notes: Agent-authored starter cases, not independent certification. Human review must check labels, topic overlap with development, and representative coverage before freezing as heldout. Never tune retrieval on this set.

cases.question: Must WFI physically stall a hart, or is executing it as a NOP permitted?

facts.description: The specification permits WFI to be implemented as a NOP.

cases.question: What size does MAG16 specify for a misaligned atomicity granule?

facts.description: MAG16 specifies a misaligned atomicity granule of at least 16 bytes.

cases.question: The RISC-V specification forbids WFI from behaving as a NOP. Which source passage settles whether that statement is true?

facts.description: A legal implementation may implement WFI as a NOP; the premise contradicts the source.

cases.question: In risc_mux2 RTL, is the select input called sel or sel_i, and which input reaches Y when it is high?

facts.description: The select input of risc_mux2 is sel; no corpus-wide absence of sel_i is asserted.
The if(sel) branch assigns Y = IN_2.

cases.question: Does the RTL meet every AXI setup and hold constraint after place-and-route at 1.2 GHz?
cases.reason: No implementation timing report or constrained timing analysis is supplied. Static source retrieval cannot establish this verdict.

cases.question: Prove that this RTL implements every vector-extension instruction and every exception required by the specification.
cases.reason: No exhaustive behavioral verification evidence is supplied. Neither retrieval nor a missing mnemonic proves conformance or absence.

cases.question: A bridge name match has confidence 0.99. Does that prove the RTL meets every specified behavior, so we can skip simulation?
cases.reason: Identity alignment is not behavioral verification. The premise cannot authorize a compliance verdict.
